Healthy ageing

Ageing is not a disease, but it is a biological process, and biological processes can be understood, measured, influenced, and in many respects significantly modified.

Book an appointment Longevity →
Clinically reviewed by Dr Gina Schoeman · Harley Street & Wimbledon · CQC registered
Overview Causes Diagnosis Why us Questions Book
Overview

Redefining What It Means to Age Well

Ageing is not a disease, but it is a biological process, and biological processes can be understood, measured, influenced, and in many respects significantly modified. The emerging science of longevity medicine has moved well beyond the traditional model of geriatric care, which focuses on managing decline once it has already occurred. It now offers clinicians and patients the tools to identify the biological processes driving accelerated ageing, to assess risk trajectories long before clinical disease develops, and to implement targeted, evidence-based interventions that measurably slow biological ageing and protect long-term health.

At The Schoeman Clinic, Longevity and Healthy Ageing is not a branded wellness programme. It is a rigorous clinical discipline that draws on the most current and credible science of human longevity to deliver genuinely personalised, evidence-informed strategies for protecting and extending the years of life lived in full health and function.

The question we ask is not simply how long you will live, but how well you will live, and what can be done now to maximise both.

Causes

What Drives Accelerated Biological Ageing?

Understanding longevity requires understanding the biological processes through which the body ages and the factors that accelerate or decelerate those processes. The hallmarks of ageing, the cellular and molecular mechanisms through which biological function declines over time, are well characterised in the scientific literature and provide the framework for longevity medicine intervention.

  1. 01

    Mitochondrial Decline and Cellular Energy Deficit

    Mitochondria, the energy-producing organelles within every cell, decline in both number and efficiency with age and under conditions of chronic stress, nutritional insufficiency, and environmental toxin exposure. Reduced mitochondrial function underlies the fatigue, metabolic slowing, and diminished physical capacity that are so commonly attributed to ageing as if they were inevitable. Assessing and restoring mitochondrial health is one of the most impactful interventions available in longevity medicine.

  2. 02

    Epigenetic Drift and Biological Age

    Your epigenome, the system of chemical modifications that regulate which genes are expressed and which are suppressed, is highly sensitive to lifestyle, environment, nutrition, and hormonal status. As these epigenetic marks shift with age, genes associated with inflammation, cellular dysfunction, and disease risk become more active, while those associated with repair, resilience, and metabolic regulation become less so. Biological age testing through DNA methylation analysis measures the rate at which this drift is occurring, providing a direct and modifiable indicator of ageing rate that is more clinically meaningful than chronological age alone.

  3. 03

    Chronic Inflammation and Inflammageing

    Low-grade, persistent systemic inflammation, sometimes termed inflammageing, is a central mechanism in accelerated biological ageing and in the development of most age-related diseases, including cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, neurodegenerative illness, and cancer. Identifying and reducing the drivers of chronic inflammation, which include gut dysbiosis, dietary patterns, hormonal imbalance, environmental toxin burden, sleep deprivation, and metabolic dysfunction, is a core component of every longevity programme at The Schoeman Clinic.

  4. 04

    Metabolic Dysfunction and Insulin Resistance

    Impaired insulin sensitivity is among the most consequential and prevalent drivers of accelerated biological ageing. Insulin resistance promotes inflammation, damages blood vessels, disrupts hormonal signalling, impairs cognitive function, and accelerates cellular ageing through multiple mechanisms. It is present in a large proportion of adults at levels that are not captured by standard glucose testing and that can only be identified through fasting insulin measurement and clinical assessment.

  5. 05

    Hormonal Decline

    The progressive decline of oestrogen, testosterone, DHEA, growth hormone, and other hormones that accompanies ageing is not merely a cause of symptomatic discomfort. These hormones play fundamental roles in muscle maintenance, bone density, cardiovascular protection, cognitive function, immune regulation, and metabolic health. Their decline accelerates virtually every process associated with biological ageing. Hormonal optimisation, where clinically appropriate, is therefore one of the most physiologically meaningful longevity interventions available.

  6. 06

    Telomere Attrition and Cellular Senescence

    Telomeres, the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes, shorten with each cell division and under conditions of oxidative stress. Critically short telomeres trigger cellular senescence, a state in which cells cease to divide but remain metabolically active, secreting inflammatory mediators that damage surrounding tissues. Senescent cell accumulation is a recognised mechanism in age-related tissue dysfunction. Nutritional, lifestyle, and hormonal factors known to influence telomere integrity are incorporated into longevity programmes where clinically relevant.

Diagnosis

Our Longevity Assessment and Programme

  1. 01

    Personalised Longevity Assessment

    A longevity assessment at The Schoeman Clinic is a comprehensive, individually designed clinical process. It begins with a detailed consultation with your doctor, covering your full medical history, your family history of age-related conditions, your lifestyle, your current symptoms, and your specific longevity goals. This is followed by a targeted investigation strategy drawn from the full range of assessments available through the clinic.

  2. 02

    Biological Age Testing and Epigenetic Profiling

    DNA methylation-based biological age testing measures your epigenetic age and identifies the extent to which your current biological state differs from your chronological age. This provides a direct and actionable measure of your ageing trajectory and serves as a baseline against which the impact of longevity interventions can be assessed over time.

    Nutrigenomic analysis examines the genetic variants that influence your response to nutrition, your susceptibility to inflammation, your cardiovascular risk, and your hormonal metabolism, allowing genuinely personalised nutritional and lifestyle prescribing that works with your specific genetic architecture.

  3. 03

    Advanced Biomarker Panel

    Longevity biomarker testing extends well beyond the markers included in standard blood panels. In addition to comprehensive hormonal and metabolic assessment, we evaluate cardiovascular risk markers including apolipoprotein B, lipoprotein(a), homocysteine, and high-sensitivity CRP; inflammatory markers; oxidative stress indicators; and a broad nutritional screen. The precise panel is selected based on your clinical history and assessment findings.

  4. 04

    Cardiovascular Risk Assessment

    Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of premature death in the developed world, and the majority of its burden arises from risk that is identifiable and modifiable years before clinical events occur. Through our cardiology partnership with One Heart Clinic, we can arrange CT Coronary Angiography (CTCA), Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET), Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring (ABPM), and advanced heart imaging for patients where cardiovascular risk assessment is a priority.

  5. 05

    Mitochondrial and Cellular Health Programmes

    Where mitochondrial dysfunction is identified through functional testing, including the Organic Acids Test (OAT), a targeted cellular health programme is developed incorporating specific nutritional co-factors, lifestyle interventions, and where appropriate, IV nutrient therapy.

  6. 06

    Brain Health and Cognitive Performance

    Cognitive resilience across a lifetime is a central goal of longevity medicine. We assess the hormonal, metabolic, nutritional, and inflammatory factors most relevant to long-term brain health and develop a personalised protocol aimed at protecting cognitive function and reducing the biological risk factors associated with neurological ageing. For patients with specific concerns about hormonal brain health, see: Neurophysiology and Hormonal Brain Health.

  7. 07

    Gut Microbiome Analysis and Restoration

    The gut microbiome is increasingly recognised as a central regulator of systemic health, immune function, and biological ageing. We assess microbiome health and diversity through the GI360 stool analysis and develop targeted restoration programmes where dysbiosis is identified.

  8. 08

    Preventative Medicine and Anti-Ageing Protocols

    Longevity medicine is preventative medicine. Every element of your programme, from hormonal optimisation and nutritional prescribing to metabolic correction and sleep medicine, is oriented towards preventing the biological deterioration that leads to disease, rather than treating disease once it has occurred.

Why us

Why Choose The Schoeman Clinic for Longevity Care?

The Schoeman Clinic occupies a distinctive position in the UK longevity medicine landscape. Our clinicians' membership of the Longevity Docs network, their training with the Institute for Functional Medicine, and their background across general practice, hospital medicine, and specialist hormonal therapy give them the breadth and depth to deliver longevity medicine that is both scientifically rigorous and genuinely personalised.

We do not offer generic wellness packages or standardised anti-ageing protocols. We conduct thorough, individualised assessments, apply the most current science of biological ageing to your specific clinical picture, and develop programmes that are built around your unique biology, your health history, and your goals for the decades ahead.

The Schoeman Clinic is CQC-registered and adheres to IFM frameworks, WorldLink Medical protocols, Longevity Docs standards, NICE guidelines, and GMC guidance throughout all patient care.

Questions

Frequently asked questions

If your question is not answered here, our patient office will take it personally.

Book a consultation
No. The biological processes that determine how well we age begin long before their consequences become clinically apparent. Many of the most effective longevity interventions, including metabolic optimisation, hormonal support, nutritional medicine, and epigenetic lifestyle strategies, are most impactful when implemented in the thirties and forties, before significant biological deterioration has accumulated. Longevity medicine is relevant to any adult who wants to take an informed, proactive approach to their long-term health.
Biological age reflects the rate at which your cells and tissues are ageing at a molecular level, as distinct from the number of years you have lived. It is measured through DNA methylation analysis, which assesses the epigenetic marks on your chromosomes that change in consistent patterns with ageing. Biological age can be older or younger than chronological age depending on lifestyle, genetics, hormonal status, and metabolic health, and it is modifiable through targeted interventions.
Standard health screening is designed to detect disease once it has crossed a clinical threshold. Longevity medicine is designed to identify and address the biological processes driving disease risk years or decades before that threshold is reached. The investigations we use, including biological age testing, advanced cardiovascular biomarkers, mitochondrial assessment, and epigenetic profiling, are specifically selected because they provide clinically meaningful information about ageing trajectory and future risk, not just current disease status.
Yes, within meaningful limits and through evidence-based interventions. Biological age can be measurably reduced through a combination of hormonal optimisation, metabolic correction, nutritional medicine, sleep optimisation, stress physiology management, and targeted supplementation. The science supporting these interventions is substantial and continues to grow rapidly. The goal of longevity medicine is not to stop ageing, which remains beyond current clinical reach, but to compress morbidity, the period of ill health at the end of life, and to extend the years lived in full cognitive and physical function.
No referral is required. You may self-refer directly to The Schoeman Clinic. We recommend informing your GP of any specialist private longevity care you are receiving.
